Question: Explain the law of demand and distinguish between a movement along and a shift of the demand curve.
reference_answer: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded falls as price rises. A price change causes movement along the curve; changes in income, tastes, prices of related goods or expectations shift the whole curve.
keywords: law of demand, demand curve, movement along, shift, determinants

Question: Calculate price elasticity of demand using the percentage method when price rises from Rs 10 to Rs 12 and quantity falls from 100 to 80 units.
reference_answer: Percentage change in quantity = (20/100) x 100 = 20%. Percentage change in price = (2/10) x 100 = 20%. Elasticity = 20/20 = 1, so demand is unit elastic.
keywords: price elasticity, percentage method, quantity demanded, unit elastic

Question: Explain the expenditure method of estimating national income with its main components.
reference_answer: Expenditure method adds final consumption expenditure, gross domestic capital formation, government final consumption expenditure and net exports. It avoids double counting by including only final goods and services produced within the domestic territory during a year.
keywords: national income, expenditure method, consumption, investment, government expenditure, net exports

Question: Discuss the functions of money and the role of a central bank in controlling credit.
reference_answer: Money acts as a medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value and standard of deferred payment. A central bank controls credit through the repo rate, cash reserve ratio, open market operations and moral suasion.
keywords: money, medium of exchange, central bank, credit control, repo rate, CRR
